title: The Covenant of Mykkiel
subtitle: The Faith Founded on a Verdict

lore.description: Every other faith in the Amaranthine begins with a message. The Covenant begins with a ruling. It does not hold that a messenger came down with words to be recited; it holds that a woman of the Sidhi diaspora, dispossessed and without recourse, brought a grievance — and that Mykkiel, the Arbiter, heard the case and found for her. The founding document of the faith is not a revelation. It is a judgment, with a plaintiff, a respondent, findings and a remedy. The first Covenanter was not a prophet. She was a litigant, and she won, and the faith has never entirely recovered from the confidence of that.
lore.followers: Mykkiel, called the Arbiter, is the living seal of this contract. He does not create law; he remembers it. His followers are judges, not legislators. They do not interpret the Covenant; they apply it. There is a terrible beauty in that. There is also a terrible coldness.

names_across_regions.pereshi: The Covenant, the ancient law of the highlands and trade routes
names_across_regions.galanina: The Grand Ledger's Faith, centered around the brass-bound book in the vault
names_across_regions.ashaan: The Oath-Keeper, viewed with suspicion by the Veiled Sisters' remnants
names_across_regions.thepyrgos: The Law-Bringers, mediators in disputes between the Two Fires

lore.quote: We were not told. We were heard, and the finding was entered.

domain_focus: The Divine Contract: the universe is an agreement; those who honor it align with reality
The Role of Mykkiel: the Arbiter, the living seal of the Covenant
The Grand Ledger: every judgment recorded; a name struck from it is struck from the community
The Unspoken Ninth Clause: a ruling that was never recorded—judgment without presence
doctrines: The universe is a contract. In the beginning, the great powers entered into a binding agreement to govern chaos.
Those who honor the Covenant align themselves with the fundamental structure of reality.
Those who break the Covenant become dissonant, unmoored, and eventually erased by the world's rejection.
Mykkiel does not create law; he remembers it. His followers are judges, not legislators.
practices: Worship is conducted in courts, not temples. A service involves reading a case, hearing testimony, and pronouncing judgment.
Every judgment is recorded in the Grand Ledger, a brass-bound book kept in a vault in Galanina.
A name struck from the Ledger is struck from the Covenant community—they may be treated as outlaws.
The Unspoken Ninth Clause allows trials in absentia—condemning the dead, the exiled, and the unreachable.

hierarchy.order_of_mykkiel: Judges, notaries, and law-scholars. They settle disputes, draft contracts, and administer the Covenant Courts. Hierarchical, with High Justiciars at the top and Circuit Judges who travel the roads.
hierarchy.order_of_the_inquisitor_prime: The Accuser—the one who brings hidden sins to light. They investigate broken oaths, expose secret perjury, and demand restitution. Secretive and decentralized. Identified by their iron scales and violet sash.
hierarchy.order_of_the_oath_of_flame__light: Healers with a contract: the patient must swear to live a more lawful life. Healing always comes with a binding agreement.

orders.name: The Order of Mykkiel
orders.description: The orthodox judges, notaries, and law-scholars. They settle disputes, draft contracts, and administer the Covenant Courts. Their authority is recognized wherever trade and treaties require a trusted third party.

orders.name: The Order of the Inquisitor Prime
orders.description: The Accuser—the one who brings hidden sins to light. They investigate broken oaths, expose secret perjury, and demand restitution. Their Rites are those of revelation and correction. They carry no swords—only iron scales and a copy of the Canons of Obligation.

orders.name: The Order of the Oath of Flame & Light (Hospitalier)
orders.description: In the Covenant, the Oath of Flame & Light is not a warrior's path but a healer's. They tend to the wounded in body and soul, but their healing always comes with a contract: the patient must swear to live a more lawful life. Their Rites are those of purification, cleansing, and bound mercy.

relationship_to_patrons.mykkiel: The Arbiter—the living seal of the Covenant. His followers are judges, not legislators.
relationship_to_patrons.inquisitor_prime: The Accuser—the one who brings hidden sins to light. They investigate and expose, but do not execute.
relationship_to_patrons.oath_of_flame__light: The Healer with a contract—healing always comes with a binding agreement to live a lawful life.

relationship_to_two_fires.cooperation: Shared inquisitions: when a heretic flees across borders, the Covenant's Inquisitors, the Everflame's Flame-Wardens, and the Temple's Chain-Lanterns may coordinate pursuit. The cooperation is transactional but effective.
relationship_to_two_fires.conflict: Jurisdiction disputes: the Covenant claims universal authority over all oaths and contracts. The Everflame claims universal authority over all heresy. The Temple claims universal authority over all miracles. When a case involves all three, no one can agree on who has jurisdiction.

crusades.ashaan_crusade: The Ashaan Crusade (890–901 AR) was the largest military expedition in modern memory. Three faiths—the Everflame, the Temple of Light, and the Covenant—joined forces to liberate the Pereshi highlands from the Veiled Sisters. The Covenant was the driving force behind the Crusade. Its judges had long memories of the Veiled Sisters' crimes.
crusades.linn_crusade: The Linn Crusade is not a military campaign—it is a Crusade of education, conversion, and cultural replacement. The Temple sends teachers, healers, and grain. The Everflame sends missionaries, guards, and basilicas. The Covenant sends judges and notaries, offering to mediate disputes between the two.
crusades.doctrine: The Covenant views Crusades as properly ordered violence—a form of law enforcement on a divine scale. A Crusade is not a war of conquest but a judgment: a verdict pronounced by the divine, executed by the faithful.

the_ninth_clause.description: The Unspoken Ninth Clause is a ruling that was never recorded—a judgment that exists only in the memory of the judge who pronounced it. The ruling holds that 'in cases where the accused is not present, and no witness can be found, the judge may pronounce judgment based on the weight of testimony already recorded.'
the_ninth_clause.uses: Justifies trials in absentia—condemning the dead, the exiled, and the unreachable. Also used to justify preemptive judgment—convicting someone before they have committed the crime.
the_ninth_clause.secrecy: The Covenant's orthodox authorities deny that the Unspoken Ninth Clause exists. They know that it does. The clause is a secret passed from judge to judge, never written down, but always remembered.

adventure_seed.title: The Missing Ledger
adventure_seed.description: A Covenant Circuit Judge has vanished while investigating a series of broken oaths in the Mistlands. The judge's ledger, containing sensitive testimony, is missing. The party must find the judge—or the ledger—before the Chain-Lanterns do. The ledger contains names that could destabilize the fragile peace between the Two Fires.
adventure_seed.quote: The Covenant is not a third fire—it is a ledger. It does not seek to burn or illuminate; it seeks to record. In a world of schism and crusade, the Covenant offers a different path: one of law, duty, and the weight of the word spoken and kept.

sample_npc.name: A Covenant Judge
sample_npc.description: A judge who carries an iron seal and a copy of the Canons of Obligation. They do not smile. They do not weep. They weigh testimony, pronounce judgment, and strike names from the Grand Ledger. The silence in their court is heavier than any flame.

founding.description: The Covenant has no messenger-angel and is proud of it. To a Covenanter, a faith founded on a recitation asks you to believe a speaker; a faith founded on a verdict asks you to read the reasoning and check it. Covenant children are taught the founding judgment the way Temple children are taught letters: as a text you are expected to argue with. The accusation that a faith without a messenger is a faith without a word from on high has been made by the Everflame for three centuries and still lands, which is why Covenant scholars answer it at such length.

salvation.name: Standing
salvation.shape: A status under the terms, not a state of the soul.
salvation.description: One is not purified and not personally met. One is either in good faith under the covenant or in breach of it, and either condition can be argued, evidenced and cured. Breach is remediable; what is not remediable is refusing to appear.
salvation.why_it_is_beautiful: The Covenant will hear anyone. Its courts take the case of a servant against a house, a wife against a husband, a tenant against a landlord — seriously, for free — and their judgments have been enforced against people who were confident they could not be. In three regions the Covenant is the only body that will write down what a poor person says and treat the writing as binding.
salvation.why_it_is_terrible: A faith founded on a winning verdict believes it has already prevailed, and treats every disagreement as an appeal it expects to dismiss. Its judgments bind the losing side absolutely and forever, including descendants who were not present. Its formal position is that the unbound are not wicked but unheard, which sounds gentle until you notice that it makes the rest of the world a list of matters not yet reached.

beauty: Courts that will hear a servant against a house, for free, and mean it.
A founding text every child is taught to argue with rather than recite.
The Accuser's standing duty to bring the case against the faith's own officers when the case is good.
Hospitallers who have spent two centuries arguing how small a healing's terms may honourably be, and have got it down to a promise to eat.
ugliness: Judgments that bind the descendants of the losing party, who were not present and cannot appeal.
The certainty of a faith that opened with a win, and answers dissent as though it were a rehearing.
Standing that can be lost on a technicality argued by people who were trained to argue technicalities.
Its total absence of a mercy Order, which its rivals never stop mentioning and its own healers quietly resent.
orders_are_masks: An Order is not a department of this faith. It is the shape a specific Patron takes inside it — the office through which that presence is approached, named and made respectable. This is why the same Order appears in faiths that despise each other, and why it does not hold the same rank in each. Where an Order sits in the hierarchy is a claim about what the faith is for, and most schisms begin as a quarrel over which Order speaks first.

internal_schism.name: The Recusants
internal_schism.claim: A judge who founds a faith cannot then preside over it.
internal_schism.description: They hold that Mykkiel is obliged to recuse himself from all matters touching the Covenant. Nobody has found the flaw in the argument and nobody with a position will say so aloud. Recusant congregations keep an empty seat on the bench, and are considered either the most rigorous Covenanters alive or a nest of sophists, depending entirely on who is asked.
